name: Midianites
summary: Descendants of Abraham through Keturah: caravan traders and camel-riding nomads of north-western Arabia. A Midianite caravan carried Joseph to Egypt, and Moses found refuge, a wife and a wise father-in-law among them. Later, Midianite hordes 'as grasshoppers for multitude' were routed by Gideon's three hundred.

origin.account: After Sarah's death Abraham married Keturah, who bore six sons including Midian. Abraham gave gifts to these sons and sent them 'eastward, unto the east country', away from Isaac.

lineage.ancestor: Midian, son of Abraham and Keturah
lineage.notes: Midian's sons were Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida and Eldaah. The Kenites seem to have been a Midianite clan: Moses' father-in-law is 'the priest of Midian' and also 'the Kenite'. The Bible uses 'Midianites' and 'Ishmaelites' for the same traders in the Joseph story and in Judges 8:24.

homeland.region: Midian — north-western Arabia, east of the Gulf of Aqaba
homeland.description: Mountain and desert country in the northern Hejaz, with oases and trade routes, from where the Midianites ranged into Sinai, Moab and the Jordan valley. They were famed for camels and for wealth in gold ornaments.
homeland.modern_location: North-western Saudi Arabia (Tabuk region), with ranges into southern Jordan and Sinai.

places.name: Land of Midian
places.note: Where Moses kept Jethro's flock (al-Bad' has a traditional 'Wells of Moses').

places.name: Qurayyah
places.note: Walled oasis town that gives its name to 'Midianite' (Qurayyah) painted pottery.

places.name: Valley of Jezreel / hill of Moreh
Timna
places.note: Copper mining site with a Midianite-period tent shrine (not named in the Bible).

timeline.event: Midian born to Abraham and Keturah; the family is sent east.
Midianite merchantmen draw Joseph out of the pit and sell him into Egypt.
Moses flees Pharaoh to Midian, marries Zipporah daughter of Reuel/Jethro, and meets God at the burning bush.
Jethro visits Moses, rejoices at the Exodus, and advises him to appoint judges. Moses asks Hobab to be Israel's guide.
Midian's elders join Balak in hiring Balaam; Midianite women lead Israel into sin at Peor. Israel wars against Midian and Balaam is killed.
Midian and the 'children of the east' plunder Israel for seven years. Gideon's 300 rout them with trumpets, pitchers and lamps; the princes Oreb and Zeeb and the kings Zebah and Zalmunna are killed.
'The day of Midian' becomes the prophets' byword for God's sudden deliverance; Midian's camels are foreseen bringing gifts to Zion.
Stephen recalls Moses as 'a stranger in the land of Madian'.

religion.practices: The Bible shows two sides of Midian. Jethro, 'the priest of Midian', confessed 'Now I know that the LORD is greater than all gods' and offered sacrifices with Aaron and the elders. The Midianites who joined Moab worshipped Baal-peor. At Timna a Midianite-era tent shrine held a small copper serpent.

importance: Midian is where God prepared Moses. The prince of Egypt spent forty years there as a shepherd, and there God spoke from the burning bush and revealed His name, 'I AM THAT I AM'. A Midianite priest gave Israel its first system of judges. Later, Gideon's victory over Midian became Scripture's classic lesson that God saves 'not by many' but by His own power, so that Israel could not boast 'Mine own hand hath saved me.'

impact.how: Sold by his brothers to a Midianite caravan and carried to Egypt, the start of God's plan to 'save much people alive'.
Found refuge, family, a shepherd's training and his call in Midian.
Jethro's counsel created rulers of thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens.
His zeal against Zimri and the Midianite Cozbi stopped the plague and won an everlasting priesthood.
The least in his father's house became Israel's deliverer through God's reduction of the army from 32,000 to 300.

notable_people.name: Hobab
notable_people.role: Moses' brother-in-law, invited to guide Israel

notable_people.name: Oreb, Zeeb, Zebah and Zalmunna
notable_people.role: Princes and kings defeated by Gideon

key_verses.text: And she bare him Zimran, and Jokshan, and Medan, and Midian, and Ishbak, and Shuah.
Now when Pharaoh heard this thing, he sought to slay Moses. But Moses fled from the face of Pharaoh, and dwelt in the land of Midian: and he sat down by a well.
Now I know that the LORD is greater than all gods: for in the thing wherein they dealt proudly he was above them.
And the LORD said unto Gideon, The people that are with thee are too many for me to give the Midianites into their hands, lest Israel vaunt themselves against me, saying, Mine own hand hath saved me.
For thou hast broken the yoke of his burden, and the staff of his shoulder, the rod of his oppressor, as in the day of Midian.

fate.summary: After Gideon, Midian 'lifted up their heads no more'. The Midianites fade from history, absorbed into the Arab tribes of northern Arabia. Classical and early Islamic geographers still knew a town called Madyan on the Gulf of Aqaba coast.

today.summary: No Midianite people exist today. Their land is in Saudi Arabia's Tabuk province, where the town of al-Bad' has traditionally been identified with Madyan. The Quran knows the people of 'Madyan' and their prophet Shu'ayb, whom Muslim tradition often links with Jethro.
today.descendants: Absorbed into the Arab tribes of northern Arabia.
today.modern_legacy: The 'Midianite–Kenite hypothesis', which proposes that Israel's worship of YHWH had roots in Midian through Jethro, is widely discussed in biblical scholarship and disputed.

archaeology.name: Qurayyah painted ware ('Midianite pottery')
archaeology.discovered: Qurayyah and sites in the Arabah, Negev and southern Jordan
archaeology.significance: Distinctive pottery tracing Midianite trade and presence.

archaeology.name: Timna tent shrine and copper serpent
archaeology.location: Timna Valley; Eretz Israel Museum, Tel Aviv
archaeology.significance: A Midianite-period shrine in an Egyptian mining temple, with a small gilded copper snake — often compared to Moses' brazen serpent.
